must_establish: An N-point DFT is a complete coordinate transform for one declared N-sample record, not a detector that returns only physically present sinusoids.
Under the house convention, the DFT is the finite-record DTFT sampled at omega_k=2 pi k/N.
A bin has normalized angular frequency before it has hertz; hertz requires both f_s and N.
Real records give conjugate-symmetric coefficients, with DC and, only for even N, Nyquist as self-conjugate real singletons.
Raw two-sided coefficients, one-sided peak amplitudes, unitary coefficients, and packed storage are different objects and need separate ledgers.
Pointwise multiplication of two N-point DFTs followed by the declared IDFT gives N-point circular convolution; zero padding to N >= L_x+L_h-1 embeds linear convolution exactly.
Zero padding samples the same finite-record DTFT more densely; genuinely longer data can improve discrimination, while appended zeros cannot add resolving information.
must_not_expand: Do not teach FFT factorization beyond the final even/odd handoff.
Do not turn the lesson into peak estimation, window selection, or streaming FFT convolution; those have later lessons.
Do not infer periodic physical data from a finite record. Periodicity belongs to the DFT representation/circular indexing unless the acquisition model separately asserts it.
recommended_body_sequence: Freeze indices, sign, scale, endpoint, and unit conventions before the first calculation.
Relate the declared DFT to DTFT samples and correlations against orthogonal basis rows.
Compute one complete short transform and map bins to normalized and physical frequency.
Derive real-input symmetry and treat DC/even-N Nyquist boundaries.
Give a two-sided/one-sided/scaling/storage ledger with reconstruction and amplitude use cases.
Derive circular convolution and the exact zero-padding condition.
Use the padding-versus-data comparison, then close with the even/odd FFT split.

frozen_conventions.record: x[n] is declared only for integer n=0,...,N-1 unless an extension is explicitly supplied.
frozen_conventions.root: W_N = exp(-j 2 pi/N), so X[k]=sum_n x[n] W_N^{kn}.
frozen_conventions.dtft_sampling: For the zero-extended finite record X_r(e^{j omega})=sum_{n=0}^{N-1}x[n]exp(-j omega n), X[k]=X_r(e^{j omega}) at omega=2 pi k/N.
frozen_conventions.unshifted_frequency: omega_k=2 pi k/N rad/sample and f_k=k f_s/N Hz for k=0,...,N-1; bins above Nyquist are equivalent negative-frequency representatives, not additional frequencies above f_s/2.
frozen_conventions.signed_frequency: Use the half-open interval [-pi,pi): kappa(k)=k for k<N/2 and kappa(k)=k-N for k>=N/2; omega_tilde=2 pi kappa/N and f_tilde=kappa f_s/N. Thus an even-N Nyquist bin is labeled -pi or -f_s/2 in this signed ledger. If a figure instead labels it +f_s/2, state that endpoint choice and do not show both.
frozen_conventions.record_time: Sample locations 0 through (N-1)T_s span (N-1)T_s, while the periodized N-sample block and bin spacing use period N T_s; do not call both quantities 'record duration' without qualification.
frozen_conventions.phase: Use principal phase in (-pi,pi] with -pi represented as +pi, inherited from the concept ledger. Phase is undefined when X[k]=0.
frozen_conventions.circular_convolution: (x circular_N h)[n]=sum_{m=0}^{N-1}x[m]h[(n-m) mod N]. Under the house DFT pair, DFT{x circular_N h}=X[k]H[k].
frozen_conventions.one_sided_peak_amplitude: For real x under the raw forward DFT, A[0]=|X[0]|/N; if N is even, A[N/2]=|X[N/2]|/N; every other retained positive-frequency bin uses A[k]=2|X[k]|/N. Odd N has no Nyquist singleton.
frozen_conventions.unitary_alternative: If both directions use 1/sqrt(N), label the coefficients X_u=X/sqrt(N); then sum|x|^2=sum|X_u|^2. Do not mix this with the house pair inside an example.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.claim: sum_{n=0}^{N-1} exp(j2 pi (k-l)n/N)=N when k=l mod N and 0 otherwise; hence the inverse kernel is the conjugate forward kernel scaled by 1/N.
With v_k[n]=exp(j2 pi kn/N), X[k]=<x,v_k>=sum_n x[n]conj(v_k[n]); it is a complex coordinate/correlation, not a yes/no physical-tone test.
Substitution of omega=2 pi k/N into the finite-record DTFT yields the declared DFT exactly.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.qualification: This is the DTFT of the declared finite record. Zero padding changes the sampling grid but not that finite sum.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.derivation: For real x[n], X[(N-k) mod N]=sum_n x[n]exp(+j2 pi kn/N)=conj(X[k]).
checked_claims_formulas_examples.boundaries: X[0] is real. For even N, X[N/2] is also real. For odd N there is no Nyquist bin.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.claim: Even N retains k=0,...,N/2 (N/2+1 complex slots with real singleton endpoints); odd N retains k=0,...,(N-1)/2 ((N+1)/2 slots, only DC a singleton).

checked_claims_formulas_examples.signed_bins_hz: [0,2,-4,-2] kHz under the frozen half-open convention.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.interpretation: The nonzero pair is at +/-2 kHz; bin 2 is the -4 kHz Nyquist singleton but is zero here.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.input: x[n]=cos(2 pi n/8), f_s=8 kHz, N=8
checked_claims_formulas_examples.raw_dft: X[1]=X[7]=4; all other bins are zero.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.two_sided_use: Retain complex X[0..7] for the ordinary IDFT or coefficient multiplication; the two 0.5-amplitude complex exponentials sum to the real cosine.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.one_sided_use: The one-sided peak-amplitude ledger reports A[1]=2|4|/8=1. It is a reporting transform, not input to the ordinary length-8 IDFT.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.phase_note: A packed one-sided complex rFFT can reconstruct real input when its layout and original N are known; an amplitude-only one-sided display cannot reconstruct phase.

cases: N=1: X[0]=x[0]; DC is the only singleton and must not be doubled.
x[n]=C: X[0]=NC and all other bins vanish.
Even N, x[n]=A(-1)^n: X[N/2]=NA only; the Nyquist singleton must not be doubled.
Odd N: no sample sequence exp(j pi n) is periodic with odd period N, so a truncated alternating record is not a Nyquist-bin singleton and generally leaks.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.conclusion: A record containing one sinusoid can have nonzero values in every DFT bin; bins are coordinates/samples of the windowed record spectrum, not a list restricted to generating sinusoids.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.claim: A bin-centered real cosine of peak amplitude A away from DC/Nyquist gives conjugate magnitudes AN/2; a complex exponential of amplitude A gives one magnitude AN; a constant D gives X[0]=DN.
Doubling only paired interior magnitudes preserves peak-amplitude reporting. DC and the even-N Nyquist bin each represent their own conjugate and are never doubled.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.qualification: Power/PSD and RMS spectra require different square/frequency-width scaling and are outside this lesson unless explicitly derived.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.derivation: Insert the 1/N inverse into sum_n x[n]conj(x[n]); root orthogonality removes k!=l cross terms, leaving (1/N)sum_k|X[k]|^2.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.short_check: For x=[1,0,-1,0], time energy is 2 and spectral energy is (1/4)(|2|^2+|2|^2)=2.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.derivation: Expand DFT{x circular_N h}, substitute r=(n-m) mod N, and separate the finite periodic sums to obtain X[k]H[k].

checked_claims_formulas_examples.three_point_circular: [4,3,5], because the linear tail 3 wraps onto index 0.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.claim: For arrays of declared lengths L_x and L_h beginning at zero, the allocated linear-convolution length is L_x+L_h-1. Padding both to any N at least that large prevents modulo-N overlap.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.qualification: Actual mathematical support can be shorter if endpoints vanish or cancel, but the array-length guarantee remains the safe implementation rule.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.claim: Appending M-N zeros and taking an M-point DFT evaluates the same N-term finite-record DTFT at omega=2 pi k/M. It can reduce grid-quantized peak-location error but does not narrow the record's main lobe or create a second resolvable component.
For even N, E[k]=DFT_{N/2}{x[2r]}, O[k]=DFT_{N/2}{x[2r+1]}, X[k]=E[k]+W_N^k O[k], and X[k+N/2]=E[k]-W_N^k O[k] for k=0,...,N/2-1.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.n8_delivery: The eight-sample exercise must expose two reused four-point sums and end with a Ref to fft-factorization-and-layout; cost claims beyond this split belong to that lesson.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.claim: For forward scale alpha and inverse scale beta with alpha beta N=1, Parseval is sum|x|^2=(1/(N|alpha|^2))sum|X_alpha|^2 and DFT_alpha{x circular h}=X_alpha H_alpha/alpha.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.lesson_use: Keep alpha=1, beta=1/N in the main line; use this identity only to explain why formulas change across conventions.

inherited: DTFT sign is negative in analysis and omega is radians/sample modulo 2 pi.
A finite record does not itself declare zero or periodic extension.
For real sequences the DTFT is conjugate symmetric; phase is undefined at zeros; 0 and pi modulo 2 pi are self-conjugate frequencies.
checked_claims_formulas_examples.handoff: The prerequisite explicitly reserves circular convolution for this DFT lesson, so the distinction is continuous and nonduplicative.

checked_claims_formulas_examples.result: verified against the exact local shards and read sidecars; corrected routes are recorded under sources and issues

representation_ledger.safe_use: signed-frequency plots; reordering is not a new transform

representation_ledger.shape: API dependent; may be complex half-spectrum or real interleaving/in-place packing

conceptual_pass_conditions: The unpadded and zero-padded curves use exactly the same nonzero samples and differ only in the evaluation grid.
Peak-location error is reported in original-bin units Delta f_0=f_s/N_data, not padded-bin units.
The genuinely longer-data case adds measured samples over a longer observation; it does not reuse appended zeros.
The two-tone decision is evaluated under at least one declared relative-phase perturbation and requires two local maxima associated with the two true tones.

issues.detail: The course spec supplies outcome phrases but no reproducible signals, record lengths, padding sweep, peak rule, or phase-perturbation set. A writer may explain the result, but component implementation and numeric pass/fail evidence require those values to be frozen.

The brief's source list names Schaedler Lessons 15 and 21-23, while its own library-layout figure depends on Lesson 28 and the padding/data distinction depends on Lessons 24-25. Add Lessons 24-25 and 28 to the lesson reference route.

Lesson 28 says to divide by N/2 somewhere in an FFT/IFFT round trip. N/2 explains the raw magnitude of a bin-centered real sinusoid pair, not universal inversion. The declared raw-forward/1/N-inverse pair needs overall round-trip factor 1/N; the lesson must correct rather than repeat the source.
MIT Sessions 17-18 present DTFS analysis with 1/N and synthesis without a factor. The course convention reverses that placement. State X[k]=N a_k before borrowing MIT's matrices or examples.

The brief asks for frequency ordering but does not select whether the even-N Nyquist endpoint appears at +f_s/2 or -f_s/2. This preflight freezes a half-open [-f_s/2,f_s/2) ledger; any opposite figure convention must be stated and must not duplicate the singleton.

A one-sided complex real-FFT output can retain reconstructive phase, while a one-sided amplitude display discards phase and applies a factor-of-two rule. Do not call both 'positive-only spectrum'; label storage and amplitude reporting separately.

The brief cites Chapter 8 §§8.1-8.7 for the whole lesson. The exact core route is §§8.4-8.7 plus Problem 8.57; physical hertz and zero-padding interpretation require §§10.1-10.2, which should be added to the lesson reference.
